forum.title: Problem with STM32N6 Nucle USB Device CDC ACM
forum.best_answer_content:
Hi ​@Saeid ​@Gyessine

1- FSBL remains required because the boot ROM first copies and executes the FSBL, and then the FSBL initializes the system and transfers control to the Application. For instance, this usb example  [STM32CubeN6/Projects/STM32N6570-DK/Applications/USBX/Ux\_Device\_Video at main · STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeN6 · GitHub](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeN6/tree/main/Projects/STM32N6570-DK/Applications/USBX/Ux_Device_Video) uses  application context.

2- A good starting point is the CDC ACM example here: <https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeN6/blob/8ab3b6410f9d893ae7ead4a3315215210220cb37/Projects/NUCLEO-N657X0-Q/Applications/USBX/Ux_Device_CDC_ACM/FSBL/USBX/App/ux_device_cdc_acm.c#L269>

In general you may need to review memory allocation and USBX application source APIs in [ux\_device\_cdc\_acm.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeN6/blob/8ab3b6410f9d893ae7ead4a3315215210220cb37/Projects/NUCLEO-N657X0-Q/Applications/USBX/Ux_Device_CDC_ACM/FSBL/USBX/App/ux_device_cdc_acm.c#L269) : usbx\_cdc\_acm\_thread\_entry , usbx\_cdc\_acm\_write\_thread\_entry ..

If your goal is to understand the project organization, I recommend starting from the CubeN6 example structure, I recommend this article :<https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus/how-to-create-an-stm32n6-fsbl-load-and-run/ta-p/768206>

3- In principle, the CDC ACM example can run **without USBPD stack**, as long as the board is properly powered and the USB supply path is correct for your setup (including TCPP protection) .
forum.content_text:
Hi ST community

I'm working on a simple application to get USB Device CDC ACM up and running. My goal is to make my STM32N6 Nucleo board detectable by my laptop so that it appears as a Virtual COM Port under Windows Device Manager.

Here are my STM32CubeIDE settings:

**Step#1:  Clock Configuration.**

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/c0e8b1a8-f2be-4e5d-b152-5dc7f02012b7.png)![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/8878d64d-acb6-477f-a4e7-3d93afeb95c8.png)

**Step#2: Set SYS clock : HSE -? DIGBYPASS Clock Source**

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/45fec976-cf00-4f31-aca2-b84dfcad466f.png)

**Step#3:  Select TIM6, check off : Application**

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/f1e56b57-4d99-46c2-9901-3866cedb3b89.png)

**Step#4:  Select TIM6 as Timebase Source, check off : Application**

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/fd8bdd02-5be1-4b8d-9ebc-5201030fe524.png)

**Step#5:  Select USB1\_OTG\_HS, and select Internal HS Phy: Device, check off : Application**

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/e843c411-37e4-4c94-a066-4858566d0b84.png)

**Step#6:  Select Threadx  and check off Core and Mode: Application**

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/fb984808-834b-447f-96d4-df5883a82a10.png)

**Step#7:  Select USBx with the following setting :**

1. Mode: Application mode

2. Check off  Core system

3. UX Device:  Device CoreStack HS and Controllers HS

4. Device Class HS: CDC\_ACM

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/bfac23c0-b145-47ea-8558-e1f83e3cf36f.png)

And here is my main.c file :

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/ce143dda-ba8c-4ca0-b17d-fb6b261d419c.png)

​​​

Here is my project folder structure.

To program the board, I've set the boot switches to DEV mode and compiled only the application code. I don't build or program the FSBL.

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/ae51a29c-3fd7-4d88-92ce-7f315e86bf1a.png)

When I connect my board to my laptop, nothing happens. There isn't a new virtual COM port.

I'd appreciate it if someone could guide me on what I'm missing here.
